scope: Las Vegas Strip poker tournaments and Strip lodging, built only from official venue and property pages. Data read on 2026-11-16; the schedule pages, structure sheets, hotel rate page and WPT structures behind the rows were re-read on 2026-11-17 and compared line by line.
policy: Every row links the official page it came from. A value that could not be confirmed from an official source is left blank and listed on the Flagged for review page. Walking minutes are Google Maps walking estimates and are labelled as such. The guaranteed-pool-to-fee ratio is descriptive only and is not a forecast.
sessionLengthAssumption: No venue publishes a finish time. The schedule planner assumes a six-hour session plus a 30-minute transfer between venues, so every conflict it reports is an estimate.

single.label: Single entry (verified on the official sheet)
single.blurb: The official structure sheet prints one buy-in, one start flight and no re-entry, rebuy, add-on or second-flight clause.

flight.label: Multi-flight
flight.blurb: The official schedule publishes separate start flights. A player who does not bag for Day 2 may buy into another flight, so more than one entry is possible.

satellite.label: Satellite (seat prizes, not cash)
satellite.blurb: Prizes are entries into another event, not cash. Different maths: see the ratio note.

bounty.label: Bounty / PKO
bounty.blurb: Part of the guarantee is paid as bounties, so the printed guarantee is not a cash prize pool.

extra.label: Extra-spend formats (re-entry, rebuy, add-on, paid chip boost)
extra.blurb: Isolated from the single-entry list. Each format gives a way to spend more than the printed buy-in.

special.label: Restricted or team format
special.blurb: Team, female-only or age-restricted formats. They are labelled so they are never mistaken for an open single-entry event.

wpt.label: Wynn tournament series
wpt.blurb: Rows from the official WPT World Championship and Wynn Signature Series schedule PDFs.

recurring.label: Recurring daily or weekly room tournaments
recurring.blurb: A published cadence rather than a dated event.

conflict.label: Source conflict (not ranked)
conflict.blurb: The official sources disagree, so the monetary fields are left blank.

flags.title: The official WPT schedule PDF labels December 18 as both a Wednesday and a Friday
flags.detail: In the same PDF, 'Dec. 18 Wednesday' carries the No Limit Hold'em Day 1A and PLO rows while 'Dec. 18 Friday' carries the WPT World Championship Day 4 rows. The rows also run out of order, with the December 17 block printed after the December 18 Wednesday block. December 18, 2026 is a Friday, so the 'Wednesday' label is the error. The schedule dates are reproduced exactly as printed and the weekday label is flagged rather than corrected.

flags.title: Bellagio Saturday buy-in is printed three different ways on official sources
flags.detail: The poker-room page links the event as 'SATURDAYS | $1,000 NLH'; the structure PDF header reads 'NLH $1100 BUY-IN'; rule 07 of the same PDF reads 'Of the $600 Buy-in, $510 goes to the Prize Pool, $50 is Admin Fees and $40 is optional staff gratuity'. The row is therefore left blank for buy-in and guarantee and is not ranked.

flags.title: Bellagio tournament-resumption notice is undated and names July 26
flags.detail: The poker page still carries the notice 'Tournament play will resume on Saturday, July 26, beginning with the $300 PLO Double Board Bomb Pot Tournament at 2 PM PT.' No year is printed, July 26, 2026 was a Sunday, and the page highlights elsewhere say the PLO Double Bomb Pot runs nightly at 6 PM. The start time is therefore left as the page highlight value and the notice is listed as a conflict.

flags.title: Venetian NYE schedule prints 'Saturday, December 26, 2025' for three events
flags.detail: Events 5, 6 and 7 of the DeepStack Extravaganza NYE page are dated 'Saturday, December 26, 2025' even though the series runs December 24, 2026 to January 10, 2027. The page also misspells 'Tuesaday'. The rows are kept at 2026-12-26 and the printed label is flagged here.

flags.title: Structure sheet 13 cross-references the wrong companion sheet
flags.detail: Sheet 12 covers 'Day A+C+E' and points to 'SEE OTHER STRUCTURE SHEET FOR DAYS B+D+F'. Sheet 13 covers 'Day B+D' but points to 'SEE OTHER STRUCTURE SHEET FOR DAYS A+C+F', which should read A+C+E. Sheet 14 covers Day F and points to A+B+C+D+E. The flight groups themselves agree with the schedule page; only the cross-reference is wrong.

flags.title: Two NYE events are labelled (1Day) but have a Day 2 restart on the same schedule page
flags.detail: Event 27 '$250 No Limit Hold'em 1A $75K GTD (1Day)' carries the note 'Day 1 Payouts with 5% advancing to Day 2' and a Day 2 Restart on January 6, 2027. Event 30 '$300 No Limit Hold'em 1A $100K GTD (1Day)' has a Day 2 Restart on January 10, 2027. Both are treated as multi-day.

flags.title: MGM Grand weekly schedule sheet is headed 'August Tournament Schedule'
flags.detail: The PDF linked from the MGM Grand poker-room page is titled 'MGM Grand August Tournament Schedule' while the room page itself is current. The daily slots and buy-ins are used as printed; the month label is flagged.

flags.title: MGM Grand $120 payout table does not line up with its own entry ranges

flags.detail: Sheet 33 reads '$80 of the $600 Buy-In is withheld for house fees (Rake + Staff). $10 of the $600 Buy In will be withheld as a flat fee for ... Ladies International Poker Series (LIPS). Prize pool consists of $510 of every $600 Buy In.' Read as two separate withholdings ($80 + $10 + $510) the total is $600; read as one, it is $590. The figures are reported as printed with the ambiguity flagged.

flags.title: WPT World Championship structure sheets were not read in this pass
flags.detail: The WPT schedule PDF publishes buy-in, guarantee, chips and level length but not the entry rules. The structure PDF is an eight-chunk document. It was read on 2026-11-17 for every event starting inside the planned trip window plus the December 3-5 $1,600 event: each of those nine sheets prints an unlimited re-entry clause, so those rows are now labelled multi-entry with the printed clause attached. The WPT events outside those dates remain unread, so their rows are still marked unverified and excluded from the single-entry filter.

flags.title: The ARIA poker guide is undated and the current page asks guests to confirm by phone
flags.detail: The official guide states daily 1 PM and nightly 7 PM events but carries no date. The current poker page asks guests to call or check @ARIAPoker for whether daily events are running, and publishes no buy-in, guarantee or entry rules. The rows are kept as an undated cadence only.

flags.title: Wynn resort fee differs between published offer pages
flags.detail: The general Wynn terms used here state 'A daily resort fee of $55 plus tax'. An older, expired offer page states $50 plus tax. The actual fee on a booked reservation controls; $55 plus tax is used and the discrepancy is flagged rather than resolved.

flags.title: Only one dated checkout total exists, and it is not for the recommended trip window
flags.detail: The Venetian booking engine prints a dated total for November 17-19, 2026 with two adults: $824.25 + $55, $164.25 + $55, $146.98 tax, $1,245.48 total for a 650 sq ft Newly Remodeled Luxury King suite. For the recommended trip window of November 25 to December 2, 2026 the same engine publishes no price, so the nightly budget on this site stays at the floor computed from the published starting rates of $119 and $209 and is labelled a floor, not a quote.

flags.title: No official schedule publishes tournament finish times
flags.detail: Venetian sheets publish start time, level length and late-registration cut-off but no finish time. The overlap check therefore uses a stated planning assumption (a six-hour session plus a 30-minute transfer between venues) and every conflict it reports is an estimate, not an official statement.

flags.title: No verified start time earlier than 9:10 AM exists in the reviewed official schedules
flags.detail: The earliest verified starts are the Venetian RaceDay Stack at 10:10 AM, the Venetian seniors and tag-team events at 10:10 AM, Horseshoe at 9:00 AM and Caesars Palace at 10:00 AM, the Wynn daily at 12:00 PM and the Wynn WPT at 11:00 AM. An 'all day from 8:00 AM' plan cannot be built from official sources. The day plan therefore starts at the earliest verified start for each venue.

flags.title: Wynn daily tournaments are suspended during Wynn Signature, Wynn Millions and Classic series
flags.detail: Stated on the official poker-room page. It matters for date selection: the daily $200 and $160 events cannot be assumed to run during those windows.

flags.title: Hotel cost comparison is limited to published per-night components
flags.detail: No reviewed property publishes parking cost inside the room folio, incidentals, or the tax rate as a single checkout total, so the like-for-like comparison is built from the same published components for every property: room rate, mandatory resort fee, tax, parking and cancellation deadline.

flags.title: Horseshoe daily buy-ins, levels and guarantees are not published
flags.detail: The official Caesars page publishes six Horseshoe start times but states only that 'a mixture of buy-ins, levels and guarantees caters to all participants'. Every Horseshoe monetary field is therefore blank.

flags.title: Google Maps resolved 'Horseshoe Las Vegas' to Bally's on the first query
flags.detail: The first walking query using the property name alone was routed from Bally's Las Vegas. The figure shown for Horseshoe was re-taken using the full street address and the result is labelled as such. Walking times are Google Maps estimates captured on 2026-11-16, not venue-published figures.

flags.title: The RaceDay Stack sheets print no guarantee
flags.detail: Sheets 18 and 29 print the buy-in, rake and blind structure but no guarantee line, so events 3, 4, 5 and 6 carry a blank guarantee and are not ranked by the guaranteed-pool-to-fee ratio.

flags.title: The Ladies Championship entry fee is printed twice, differently
flags.detail: The WPT schedule prints the buy-in column as '$1,100' for 'Ladies NIH Championship (2 Day)' while the footnote under the table reads 'The Tournament Entry for the Ladies Championship is $11,100. Ladies will receive a discounted entry.' The event name is printed as 'NIH', which is a typo for No Limit Hold'em. The row keeps the printed column value and the footnote is recorded with it; nothing is adjusted.

flags.title: The '$1,000,000 Added' on the WPT World Championship is not available in Nevada
flags.detail: The schedule prints 'WPT World Championship Day 1A $1,000,000 Added' for $10,400, and the footnote under the table states: '$1,000,000 will be added in cash prizes by ClubWPT Gold. ClubWPT Gold is not available in Nevada.' The guarantee column for those rows is blank on the schedule. A Nevada player therefore cannot count the added million, which is why no guarantee is shown for those rows.

flags.title: Discounted-entry footnote markers do not resolve cleanly against the footnote list
flags.detail: The schedule prints '*', '**', '***', '****' and '*****' markers. Several rows, including the $10,500 PLO 6-Max and the $25,800 NLH High Roller, carry a four-marker footnote, while the footnote list describes the Ladies Championship entry under four markers and the general discounted entry under five. The marker is reproduced with its row and the footnote text is quoted, but the published entry is not adjusted.

flags.title: Three schedule rows on the Wynn Signature Series PDF carry an extra empty cell
flags.detail: The rows for '1/17 NLH TURBO', '1/18 NO LIMIT HOLD'EM DAY 1A' and '1/18 NLH TURBO' have one more cell than the table header, which shifts the guarantee column: the printed guarantee appears in the entry column and the entry price appears in the chip column. The values are read in the order the surrounding rows use, so the $10,000 and $100,000 figures are treated as the guarantee and $200 or $400 as the entry. The guarantee for the milestone satellites is printed as '10 Seats'.

flags.title: The official DSE schedule page misspells 'Limit' on four rows
flags.detail: The schedule page prints 'No LImit Hold'em' with a capital letter i on the rows for event 2 (November 18), event 6 (November 22), event 10 (November 25) and event 12 (November 26). The event names on this site use the corrected spelling and every row links the page and the structure sheet, so the printed label can be checked in one click.

flags.title: The Venetian booking calendar disagrees with the quote, and the cells move within a day
flags.detail: The calendar cell for November 17 read $855 in the observation recorded on 2026-11-16, while the same page's quote for the same night printed a $824.25 room rate, and an earlier observation of the same calendar on the same day recorded $605. The calendar states that its prices are the best available suite and rate, include the daily resort fee and exclude taxes. Calendar cells are logged as observations and are never used in a total.

flags.title: The official DSE IV schedule PDF prints decorative text in the DATE column on 14 rows
flags.detail: In the printable schedule PDF the DATE column of 14 rows carries promotional text instead of a weekday and date ('@PokerAtlas PRO', '@PokerAtlas* TOUR', a repeated 'CHAMPIES' line, 'LIPS FRIDAY, DECEMBER 11'). The date of each of those rows was taken from the official HTML schedule page, which prints a full date for every row, and the HTML page was re-read on 2026-11-17 with all 94 rows matching. The printed buy-in, guarantee, chip count and level length from the PDF are unaffected.

flags.title: The official DSE IV schedule PDF prints '(IDAY)' where the HTML page prints '(1Day)'
flags.detail: Several event names in the printable schedule PDF read '(IDAY)', which is the same one-day marker the HTML page prints as '(1Day)' with the numeral rendered as a capital I. The canonical rows use the HTML page's spelling. Nothing is inferred from the marker beyond the label the venue itself prints; the single-entry status on those rows comes from the structure sheet, not from the marker.

flags.title: The WPT schedule and the WPT structures sheet put the $1,600 Day 2 on different days
flags.detail: The official WPT schedule PDF prints, for the $1,600 No Limit Hold'em $1,000,000 guarantee: Dec. 3 11 a.m. Day 1A, Dec. 3 1 p.m. Day 2, Dec. 4 11 a.m. Day 1B, and no Dec. 5 row for that event. The structure sheet for the same event prints Day 1A Thursday, December 3 at 11 a.m., Day 1B Friday, December 4 at 11 a.m. and Day 2 Saturday, December 5 at 11 a.m. A Day 2 that starts two hours after its own Day 1 is not a playable sequence, so the schedule row is reproduced exactly as printed, both documents are linked from the row, and no part of the trip plan relies on it. Anyone entering this event should confirm the Day 2 date with the Wynn poker room before booking travel.

flags.title: The booking calendar publishes no price for the planned trip window
flags.detail: The official Venetian booking calendar was opened on 2026-11-17 for November 25 to December 2, 2026 with two adults, the window the plan is built on. Every date cell renders a price placeholder rather than a figure, so the only dated checkout total available anywhere on this site remains the November 17-19 quote (F15). The trip's nightly budget is therefore the published starting-rate floor of $197.28, not a quote, and the cost calculator labels it as such.

flags.title: Three further poker rooms were attempted on 2026-11-17 and publish no readable schedule page
flags.detail: The plan covers the seven Strip rooms whose official pages could be read. Three more rooms were attempted on 2026-11-17 and produced nothing publishable: the Golden Nugget poker page (https://www.goldennugget.com/las-vegas/casino/poker/) returned an empty body through the fetch path this build uses, https://www.circalasvegas.com/casino/poker is now a 404 page, and https://www.resortsworldlasvegas.com/casino/poker returns Not Found on both the short and the long-form path. No value is inferred for any of them, so they have no rows. Circa and Golden Nugget are downtown and outside the 30-minute walking limit from the Strip hotels in any case; Resorts World is on the Strip, so a later session should retry its poker page from a network that renders the venue's own page.

questions.question: Should the plan extend past the seven Strip rooms to the other Las Vegas poker rooms?
questions.answer: Not on the evidence available from the venues themselves. This build publishes the Venetian, Wynn, Bellagio, MGM Grand, Caesars Palace, Horseshoe and ARIA rooms because each of those publishes an official schedule, structure sheet or room page that could be read. The Golden Nugget poker page returned an empty body on 2026-11-17, Circa's /casino/poker path is a 404 and Resorts World's poker path returns Not Found, so those rooms have no verified rows (F33). Circa and Golden Nugget are also downtown, outside the 30-minute walking limit this trip is built on.
questions.why: Extending the list without a readable official schedule would mean either copying a third-party calendar, which the evidence policy forbids, or publishing blanks, which adds no decision value.
questions.how: Call or open the room page from a normal browser: Resorts World poker desk and the Golden Nugget daily tournament page. Anything worth adding needs a printed buy-in, start time and entry clause before it can join the single-entry list.

questions.question: What are the actual travel dates, and how many nights?
questions.answer: This session fixed the dates at November 25 to December 2, 2026 because that window holds the most single-entry events verified on an official structure sheet. The official booking engine publishes no price for those dates. The one dated checkout total it does publish is November 17-19, 2026 for two adults: $1,245.48 including the $55 nightly resort fee and $146.98 of tax.
questions.blocking: Yes - no hotel total can be confirmed without it
questions.how: Open the booking link on the hotels page with the arrival and departure dates you want; the price is printed by the venue itself.

questions.question: How many people are travelling, and is one room enough?
questions.answer: The published rates are single or double occupancy. The Venetian adds $50 plus tax per additional guest 13 and older; Bellagio adds $50 plus tax per occupant above two.
questions.blocking: Yes - occupancy changes the nightly total
questions.how: Confirm the party size and the room type before comparing totals.

questions.question: What nightly budget and quality floor apply?
questions.answer: Not supplied. No comparable official quality score exists for these rooms, so the site leaves the quality ranking blank rather than inventing one.
questions.blocking: Yes - it decides which properties are shortlisted
questions.how: Give a maximum true cost per night and the minimum standard you accept, then re-run the comparison with the published rate floors.

questions.question: Is one total entry per player actually required, or only one entry per event?
questions.answer: For the Venetian one-day events the official sheets print one buy-in, one start flight and no re-entry, rebuy, add-on or second-flight clause. The sheets never use the words 'single entry' or 'freezeout', so the site labels this as 'single entry on the official sheet' and shows the excerpt. For Wynn, Bellagio, MGM Grand and Caesars the sheets print re-entry, rebuy or add-on clauses, so those events are placed in the separate extra-spend section.
questions.blocking: No - the rule set is documented on every row
questions.how: Ask the poker room to confirm in writing that a second buy-in is not accepted for a specific event if that matters for your decision.

questions.question: Which hotels actually publish a room price for the dates you want?
questions.answer: Only The Venetian, and only through its own booking engine rather than on the rate page. For November 17-19, 2026 the engine printed $824.25 + $55, $164.25 + $55, $146.98 tax and a $1,245.48 total for a 650 sq ft Luxury King suite. Its calendar cells for November are best-available rates that include the resort fee and exclude tax, and they moved within a single day. The rate page itself still publishes only starting rates of $119 and $209, which are explicitly not date-specific, and states that rates are provided up to 150 days out.
questions.how: Open the booking link with the exact dates, then log the printed total in the rate log with its timestamp.

questions.question: Will the poker-suite rate be honoured if you play tournaments rather than cash games?
questions.answer: Yes, in writing: the rate page requires 'six hours of active live cash gameplay or buy in to a $300 or higher tournament for each night stayed', met before 2 a.m. on the last night. A $100 or $200 tournament does not qualify; a $300 or higher entry does.
questions.how: Plan at least one $300+ entry per night stayed, or accept the prevailing rate.

questions.question: How long do the tournaments actually run, so two events can be sequenced?
questions.answer: Not published. Sheets give start time, level length and the late-registration cut-off, but no finish time. The overlap check on this site uses a stated six-hour session assumption plus a 30-minute transfer, and labels every conflict as an estimate.
questions.blocking: No, but it limits the day plan
questions.how: Ask the poker room for expected finish times, or treat the plan as a template and confirm on the day.

questions.question: What is the real walking time between the chosen hotel and each poker room?
questions.answer: The venues publish no walking times. Google Maps walking estimates captured on 2026-11-16 are used and labelled as estimates: Caesars Palace to the Venetian 12 minutes, Wynn to the Venetian 13, Horseshoe 16, Bellagio 21, ARIA 31, MGM Grand 35. The Wynn poker room is in Encore, a 10-minute walk from the Wynn hotel.
questions.blocking: No - the 30-minute filter is applied to the estimates
questions.how: Re-check the live Maps route on the morning of each tournament; Strip crossings add time that the estimate does not include.

questions.question: Which other Strip rooms should be added to the plan?
questions.answer: Not covered. This pass verified The Venetian, Wynn, Bellagio, MGM Grand, Caesars Palace, Horseshoe and ARIA. South Point, Golden Nugget, Resorts World, Circa, Excalibur, Luxor, Orleans, Red Rock, Palms, Westgate, Tropicana, Bally's, Flamingo, LINQ, Planet Hollywood, Rio and M Resort were not checked.
questions.how: Say which properties to add; each needs its own official page and structure sheets.

questions.question: Do the December 17-23 and holiday-week events still run as published?
questions.answer: The schedule pages are current as published on 2026-11-16, and this site re-checks every source URL on a schedule. Any source that changes is flagged on the change log.
questions.how: Re-check the Flagged for review page and the change log before booking and again 48 hours before you travel.

questions.question: What is the cancellation deadline at each property?
questions.answer: Published and different: Wynn requires 48 hours before arrival, Bellagio 72 hours before arrival, and the Venetian bills a deposit on confirmation with blackout dates and non-refundable prepaid offers; an early checkout costs $100 plus tax.
questions.how: Use the cancellation column in the hotel table when choosing where to hold the booking.

questions.question: What does parking cost, and does it change the true cost per night?
questions.answer: Venetian: $20 per day for registered hotel guests, $20 Monday-Thursday and $25 Friday-Sunday for non-hotel guests, valet $40. Wynn: self-parking is free for registered guests and $25 per day for others, valet $40, and complimentary self-parking extends to Wynn poker-room guests. Bellagio parking was not captured in this pass.
questions.how: Include parking in the trip total if you will not stay on property every night.

suggestions.title: Publish a nightly rate snapshot per property and week
suggestions.detail: Rooms are priced per night and the published rates are only available up to 150 days out. A weekly snapshot of the official starting rate, the mandatory resort fee and the tax for each property would turn a blank column into a comparable one and would let the rate log show movement.
suggestions.decision: Needs a data source that the venue publishes without login

suggestions.title: Add a per-venue finish-time estimate that the poker room confirms
suggestions.detail: The overlap check is the weakest part of the plan because no venue publishes a finish time. A simple field on each structure sheet, confirmed by the room, would make the day plan exact instead of assumed.
suggestions.decision: Ask each poker room; the Venetian publishes structure sheets it controls

suggestions.title: Read the remaining DeepStack NYE and WPT structure sheets
suggestions.detail: Fifteen NYE sheets and the eight-chunk WPT structure PDF are still unread. Reading them would move the holiday window and the WPT week from 'schedule confirmed, rules unverified' to fully verified and would let those events into the single-entry filter.
suggestions.decision: Straightforward research, no new source needed

suggestions.title: Add the missing Strip poker rooms
suggestions.detail: South Point, Golden Nugget, Resorts World, Circa, Excalibur, Luxor, Orleans, Red Rock, Palms, Westgate, Tropicana, Bally's, Flamingo, LINQ, Planet Hollywood, Rio and M Resort are all unverified. For a trip that aims to enter as many tournaments as possible, the daily rooms in walking range are worth more than another marquee series.

suggestions.decision: Straightforward research, no new source needed

suggestions.title: Add a bankroll-versus-prize view that states the assumption
suggestions.detail: The site deliberately shows guaranteed pool divided by entry fee as a descriptive ratio and never as a forecast. A clearly labelled scenario panel could show how many buy-ins a fixed bankroll buys against a given guarantee, with the assumption written next to the number.
suggestions.decision: Whether to include any modelling at all

suggestions.title: Add a seat-availability check for the recommended day plan
suggestions.detail: The Venetian requires a Venetian Rewards card to play and the Wynn requires Wynn Rewards membership. A pre-trip checklist for rewards enrolment, and a note about MGM Rewards for Bellagio and MGM Grand, would remove a common day-of-trip failure.

suggestions.detail: Dates, nightly budget, party size and the single-entry rule are the same four inputs on every page. Storing them in the browser would let the date filter, the hotel comparison and the cost calculator agree with each other.

suggestions.title: Publish the change-detection log as a first-class page
suggestions.detail: The scheduled checker already records a dated status and content hash for every official URL. Surfacing it on its own page, with the rows that changed highlighted on the tournament tables, is what turns the site from a snapshot into something you can trust on the morning you travel.
suggestions.decision: Already implemented in this pass - confirm the presentation
